meta.about: Level 2, Canal Street: Canal St and Mott St, Chinatown, Manhattan, 7:40 PM, night, the street wet after rain. Bounds, zones, every collider, the points the game flow and the AI use, the nav layers and the art-side placements, written by the shared layout tool from the hand-authored table.
meta.name: Canal Street
meta.readFrom: the hand-authored layout table tools/levels/layouts/chinatown.py, not the web game

units.web: metres, seconds, radians; +Y up, north = -Z, east = +X (right-handed)
units.ue: centimetres, degrees; +Z up, X = east, Y = south (left-handed)

meta.conversion: ue (X, Y, Z) = web (x, z, y) * 100; ue yaw = atan2(web z, web x) of a direction = -rotationY of a prop, in degrees
meta.status: stage-1 data, unbaked: `nav.layers[*].grid` is absent until the engine bake (-run=MILevelBake) writes it; the game does not load this file yet (levels.json is unchanged)
notes: el: absent. The design has no elevated train here (chinatown.md 8.5); the loader must treat a missing `el` as no deck (MAPS.md E2). Until E2 lands, `build_level.py --el-fallback` writes a degenerate deck 250 m outside the bounds so today's loader can read the file (every deck test is a point-in-rectangle check, so it never applies).
nav: the layers, links and spawn reach are written; the grids are not. The engine bake (-run=MILevelBake) writes `nav.layers[*].grid` with FMIBoxWorld's own code.

Roof spawns rf1 to rf3 are enabled (2026-11-28): nav step A keeps a Goon on his own layer, so a Goon spawned there fights a player on the roof, and a stranded street Goon's replacement comes from there (Levels.Chinatown.RoofCamp).
Signs and screens: English only, invented names (owner's answer 2026-11-26).
deviationsFromDesign: No air points (the design's 18): the drones are removed from the game (owner, 2026-11-28).
places.regions: THE DUB ROOM (x 18..26.3, z 18..32) added before THE BANQUET HALL so the HUD names the reel's room as its objective place does (15 lists only THE BANQUET HALL for E2).
Reel 6 at x 22.2 (design 21.2, still by the racks): the leg-4 route tie's margin goes from 0.4 % to 6 %; the rest is the guidance's path hysteresis (MAPS.md G6), see guide.waivers.

ground.source: what the bare ground is made of and the walking-surface heights, as rectangles (the Block samples a 0.1 m grid; these rectangles are its source)

enemySpawns.source: authored points (docs/unreal/maps/chinatown.md). `layer` names the nav layer of a ground point; `overlooks` limits a roof point to players in those zones; `facing` is derived (toward the walkable cells it reaches in a straight line within 6 m for ground points, the centre of the level for air points): the game gives a new enemy its own yaw.

coverPoints.source: points 0.6 m out from the faces of solids 0.9 m or more tall that block shots, on a walkable cell of their layer, at least 1.2 m apart (the bake re-filters them with FMIBoxWorld)

layout.source: the layout table's named lines and rectangles (tools/levels/layouts/chinatown.py)

nav.source: layers, links and spawn reach (chinatown.md 4.4, 8.2, 15). The grids are written by the engine bake (-run=MILevelBake) with FMIBoxWorld's code, never by the layout tool: `grid` is absent until then.

guide.source: chinatown.md 7: on the street the guidance is the street layer's search, as on the Block; the route graph (MAPS.md G2) adds the yard stair (both ways) and the kitchen-roof drop onto the shed and off it (down only), so a player on the roof is drawn a walkable way down. Hints keyed by objective id live in the text overlay (frontend.story.chinatown.guide.hints)

waivers.reason: the best way out avoiding the partition door is the Mott roll-up then the Square and the arcade, 6 % longer (after Reel 6 moved 1 m east); no layout move that keeps leg 3 within 10 % of the design reaches 10 %. The guidance keeps the drawn route until another is 10 % shorter (guide.pathHysteresis), so the line cannot flip between the two inside the dub room.
